transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Meeting ID: FF-20281006-8472
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (Brightfolio Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (Brightfolio Infra), Priya Rao (Brightfolio ML)

Summary:
Quick discovery to scope an embeddings + rerank pilot. Customer evaluating where to host rerank and embedding compute (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Primary concerns: throughput (60 QPS sustained, spikes to 200), tail latency SLO (p95 200-250ms), embedding dims (384 vs 768), and data residency/KMS requirements. Discussion included vector DB integration (Faiss today), hybrid retrieval/rerank architecture, and potential fallbacks.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and constraints
- Throughput and latency targets
- Vector DB (Faiss) sharding and top-k retrieval sizing
- Rerank architecture: LLM cross-encoder vs lightweight scorer
- Hosting options: Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private VPC/on-prem
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)

Action items (discussed in call):
- Redwood to run throughput sim for Dedicated with customer sample vectors
- Brightfolio to share dataset and Faiss config
- Schedule security checklist call if pilot moves to Private

Transcript (auto-generated, medium quality, some mis-transcriptions):
[00:00:05] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE here at Redwood, and with me is Samir our solutions engineer.
[00:00:18] Alicia Gomez: Hi all, Alicia here. We're super pressed to figure out how to scale rerank without blowing our cost.
[00:00:25] Liam O'Connor: Liam, infra. We're running Faiss on EC2 today, dockerized, trying to keep PII inside our V P C.
[00:00:33] Priya Rao: Priya, ML eng, I own the embed pipeline. We're currently generating 384-d vectors using a small transformer and storing them in Faiss HNSW.
[00:00:40] Samir Patel: cool, thanks. Can you share numbers: how many vectors, what QPS, tail latency goals?
[00:00:47] Alicia Gomez: Roughly 2 million vectors, average query volume is around 60 QPS but we do daily burst windows up to maybe 180-200 QPS for short periods. P95 latency goal is about 200 to 250 ms end-to-end for our search + rerank flow.
[00:01:05] Maya Chen: helpful. And what's your current rerank approach? Full cross-encoder on all 200 results?
[00:01:12] Priya Rao: Right now we do a cheap lexical filter then retrieve top 500 from Faiss and run a transformer cross-encoder over top 200. It's... expensive. We don't have nice batching so cost is high.
[00:01:27] Liam O'Connor: We also hit oom on big bursts, so we sometimes drop rerank and fallback to lexical only which hurts relevance for SLAs.
[00:01:36] Samir Patel: okay, so typical hybrid: dense retrieval -> candidate expansion -> rerank. Two quick angles we usually push: 1) reduce vector dims or use compact embeddings (384 -> 256) if quality permits; 2) move heavyweight cross-encoder to Dedicated or Hosted with smart batching and KV cache so you get amortized token cost.
[00:01:56] Alicia Gomez: curious, how would caching work for rerank? Our queries are quite varied.
[00:02:05] Samir Patel: Good question. For rerank we often do prefix / KV caching for repeated candidates or reuse key-value cache when clients request similar contexts. Also continuous batching at the runtime level helps by grouping many small rerank calls into larger micro-batches — that reduces per-token overhead. With Dedicated you can tune batch window tightness depending on your latency budget.
[00:02:30] Priya Rao: If we do batching, how does that affect p95 tail? We can't introduce 100ms buffer to hit batching.
[00:02:36] Samir Patel: There's a tradeoff. You set batching thresholds — e.g., max latency 30ms for batching plus compute time. For p95 250ms, we can usually batch aggressively for median loads and keep a smaller window for tail-sensitive traffic; Redwood routing can prioritize low-latency lanes.
[00:02:54] Maya Chen: Also worth noting we have smart routing — you can route by policy so critical customers or endpoints hit low-latency, higher-cost lanes, and background queries go to cost-optimized lanes.
[00:03:05] Alicia Gomez: Tell me about hosting choices: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We care about cost and keeping keys in our KMS.
[00:03:13] Samir Patel: Hosted is fastest to stand up — you call our API, we handle scaling, good for proof-of-value. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with more predictable throughput and you get isolation; you can also request KMS integrations. Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane and VPC peering or on-prem installs for full data control. For keys, Private/Dedicated can support KMS or HSM integrations; Hosted can do envelope encryption but some customers prefer their own KMS.
[00:03:40] Liam O'Connor: We need SSO + SAML and audit logs for PCI scope reasons. Is that supported in Dedicated or Private?
[00:03:48] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private support SAML SSO and audit logging out of the box; Hosted can support SSO but log retention is an add-on. We'll share the SOC2 documentation as well.
[00:03:58] Priya Rao: Ok, for embedding dims — we see some quality delta going 384 -> 768 but cost doubles. Any recommendations?
[00:04:08] Samir Patel: It depends on retrieval recall needs. For most semantic search use-cases 384 often hits a good accuracy/throughput sweet spot. If you need fine-grained semantic distinctions, 768 might help, but you'd pay more in storage and QPS compute. We can run a small eval with your sample set to quantify.
[00:04:25] Alicia Gomez: That'd be great. Also, our Faiss config is tuned for HNSW with efSearch=128. We shard across 4 EC2s now. Can Redwood integrate directly with Faiss or do we need to change?
[00:04:36] Samir Patel: Redwood works with external vector DBs — we can call out to Faiss endpoints or run embeddings + rerank inside our runtime. For hybrid setups, it's common to do retrieval in your Faiss cluster then call Redwood for rerank (top-K). We also support fallback: if your Faiss latencies spike we can route to a cached top-K or a smaller approximate retrieval.
[00:04:59] Liam O'Connor: How would network hops affect latency? If we keep Faiss in our VPC and call Redwood Hosted, that's an extra hop.
[00:05:06] Samir Patel: Right, that's why some customers prefer Dedicated or Private in the same VPC/cloud region. For Hosted, you can place your Faiss cluster to call out across private link if you want lower egress. But Dedicated inside customer VPC reduces network variance.
[00:05:18] Priya Rao: Any numbers on cost per rerank query if we keep top-200 and run a cross-encoder?
[00:05:24] Samir Patel: Ballpark depends on model size and batching. Using a medium cross-encoder on Dedicated with good batching, we typically see cost reductions of 3-5x vs naive single-call setups. For Hosted at small scale cost may be higher; we'll send a modeled estimate.
[00:05:38] Alicia Gomez: We have an internal budget of roughly $0.02 per query for rerank. Is that realistic?
[00:05:43] Samir Patel: It's tight for full cross-encoder at 200 candidates but could be within reach with candidate pruning (retrieve top 200, lightweight scorer to cut to 50, cross-encoder on 50), compact embeddings, and Dedicated with aggressive batching. We'll model a couple architectures.
[00:06:00] Maya Chen: I can add two example patterns we've used in other pilots: 1) lightweight ANN + learned re-ranker (cheap rescoring) then cross-encoder on small subset; 2) full cross-encoder in Dedicated with autoscale and dedicated GPUs for burst windows. Both have different cost profiles.
[00:06:18] Alicia Gomez: Okay, demo wise what's the next step?
[00:06:22] Maya Chen: For pilot scoping let's do this: Brightfolio shares a sample export (2M vectors) and a couple of representative queries. Samir will run a Dedicated throughput sim using 384-d vectors and a hybrid architecture (retrieve 200 -> rerank 50) at 60 QPS sustained and spikes to 200. We'll return latency/cost heatmaps. Also we'll add a Hosted baseline.
[00:06:44] Priya Rao: That sim will help a lot. On compliance, we'll need SOC2 and the VPC checklist if we consider Private.
[00:06:51] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 docs and a Private/VPC checklist in the follow-up.
[00:06:56] Liam O'Connor: On infra notes: if we go Dedicated in our account, how is autoscaling handled? We can't have preemptible interruption.
[00:07:05] Samir Patel: Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools with a spec for min/max nodes and burst policies. We can set strict node replacement and capacity guarantees; it's not preemptible. For on-prem we do a different packaging but we'll discuss once we see the pilot results.
[00:07:18] Alicia Gomez: Are there customers who've done a similar 2M vector + rerank pilot?
[00:07:23] Maya Chen: Yes — a few e-commerce customers scaled to multi-million vectors with Dedicated + hybrid rerank; we can share anonymized case notes.
[00:07:30] Samir Patel: Quick caveat: quantisization and lower-bit embeddings can affect recall. We recommend running small A/B to check. And for embedding dimension-specific trade-offs we can run an offline eval comparing 256/384/768.
[00:07:46] Priya Rao: About fallback — if Faiss fails, can Redwood serve approximate results itself?
[00:07:52] Samir Patel: We have fallback policies. For Hosted you can set a fallback to a cached top-K or to a smaller model. For Dedicated/Private you can run a replicated lightweight index in Redwood runtime as backup.
[00:08:03] Liam O'Connor: Good. What about monitoring and observability — token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency?
[00:08:10] Maya Chen: Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, trace hooks and token-level cost. For Dedicated/Private consoles can be hosted behind customer SSO and we can export logs to your SIEM.
[00:08:21] Alicia Gomez: Great. Any blockers on our side to run the sim?
[00:08:26] Priya Rao: We'll need to sanitize the dataset for PII first, but we can provide an anonymized sample by Friday.
[00:08:32] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll wait for the link.

-- mid-call check --
[00:22:15] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) right, sorry, go on.
[00:22:28] Samir Patel: Back to latency numbers — if you want p99 under 400ms that's a different constraint; batching windows must be tiny and you'll need dedicated low-latency lanes.
[00:22:41] Alicia Gomez: We don't currently need p99 400 but important to know.
[00:22:45] Priya Rao: One more thing — our embeddings pipeline uses a GPU-resident model that outputs 384-d floats; would Redwood re-embed inside runtime or accept our embeddings?
[00:22:55] Samir Patel: You can bring your embeddings (we accept external vectors) or run embedding inference inside Redwood. Many customers choose to keep embeddings generation inside their infra for data control; rerank tends to be in Redwood.
[00:23:09] Liam O'Connor: If we pass vectors over to Hosted, does that trigger data retention concerns?
[00:23:15] Maya Chen: Hosted has configurable retention and data handling policies; for stricter requirements Private/Dedicated keeps more control. We'll share the retention options doc.
[00:23:23] Alicia Gomez: Let's talk about the timing — we want a decision-maker review in two weeks. Pilot would start late Oct if all good.
[00:23:31] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable — we'll aim for the sim results and cost model before your internal review.

Wrap-up / Recap:
[00:40:02] Maya Chen: Recap — Brightfolio shares anonymized 2M vector sample and example queries (Priya/Alicia). Redwood (Samir) will run Dedicated and Hosted sims for 384-d vectors, retrieve 200 -> rerank 50 pattern at 60 QPS sustained with spikes; produce latency and cost heatmaps by 2028-10-13. Maya will send pricing and SOC2/docs by 2028-10-09. We'll schedule the security deep-dive if pilot heads toward Private.
[00:40:25] Alicia Gomez: Thanks all, that works.
[00:40:28] Liam O'Connor: Thanks.
[00:40:30] Priya Rao: Thanks everyone.
[00:40:33] Maya Chen: Appreciate it — we'll follow up with notes and links. Bye!

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors and word substitutions (e.g., 'quantization' -> 'quantisization', 'KV cache' -> 'K V cash') were not corrected to preserve fidelity to the raw transcript.
